formal_statement:
namespace Hirsch

theorem polynomial_hirsch_conjecture :
    ∃ c k : ℕ, ∀ (d n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) (b : Fin n → ℝ),
      (Hpoly a b).Nonempty → Bornology.IsBounded (Hpoly a b) →
      DiamLE (Hpoly a b) (c * (n + d) ^ k) := by sorry

end Hirsch
natural_language_statement:
**The polynomial Hirsch conjecture.** There exist constants $c, k \in \mathbb{N}$ such that every nonempty bounded H-polytope $P = \{x \in \mathbb{R}^d \mid \langle a_i, x\rangle \le b_i,\ i \le n\}$ has combinatorial diameter at most $c\,(n+d)^k$: every two vertices are joined by a path of at most $c\,(n+d)^k$ edges.

Every polynomial in $n$ and $d$ is dominated by some $c(n+d)^k$ and conversely, so the statement is exactly "the diameter of a polytope is polynomially bounded in its dimension and number of defining inequalities". The original Hirsch conjecture ($n - d$) was disproved by Santos (2012); all known counterexamples violate the bound by a constant factor, while the best proven upper bounds (Kalai--Kleitman 1992, Todd 2014) are quasi-polynomial, $n^{O(\log d)}$. A positive answer is necessary for any pivot rule of the simplex method to be worst-case polynomial; the question was the subject of the Polymath 3 project.
source: Kalai, The polynomial Hirsch conjecture (Polymath 3), 2010, https://gilkalai.wordpress.com/2010/09/29/the-polynomial-hirsch-conjecture-a-proposal-for-polymath3/; survey: Santos, TOP 21 (2013), https://arxiv.org/abs/1307.5900

readback.readback:
# Read-back: `Hirsch.polynomial_hirsch_conjecture`

The statement asserts: **there exist natural numbers $c$ and $k$** (each possibly $0$) such that for **every** pair of natural numbers $d$ and $n$ (including $d = 0$ and $n = 0$), every family of vectors $a_1, \dots, a_n \in \mathbb{R}^d$ (Euclidean space of dimension $d$), and every family of reals $b_1, \dots, b_n \in \mathbb{R}$, the following holds. Let

$$P = \{\, x \in \mathbb{R}^d \mid \langle a_i, x \rangle \le b_i \text{ for all } i = 1, \dots, n \,\},$$

the solution set of the $n$ linear inequalities (this is the unfolding of the custom definition `Hpoly`; when $n = 0$ it is all of $\mathbb{R}^d$, and when $d = 0$ the ambient space is a single point). **If** $P$ is nonempty **and** $P$ is bounded (in the metric/bornology sense; closedness or compactness is not stated separately, though $P$ is an intersection of closed half-spaces), **then** the predicate $\mathrm{DiamLE}\big(P,\; c\,(n+d)^k\big)$ holds, where the bound $B = c\,(n+d)^k$ is computed in the natural numbers (in particular $(n+d)^0 = 1$, and $0^0 = 1$, so e.g. $k = 0$ gives the constant bound $c$).

Unfolding the custom definition $\mathrm{DiamLE}(P, B)$: for every $u$ and every $v$ that are **extreme points** of $P$ (points $x \in P$ such that whenever $x$ lies in the open segment between two points of $P$, both of those points equal $x$), there exists a function $w : \mathbb{N} \to \mathbb{R}^d$ with

$$w_0 = u, \qquad w_B = v,$$

and for every index $i < B$, either $w_i = w_{i+1}$ (a stationary step) or $w_i$ and $w_{i+1}$ are **adjacent** on $P$ in the sense of the custom definition `Adj`. Only the values $w_0, \dots, w_B$ are constrained; the intermediate points $w_i$ are not themselves required to be extreme points or even to lie in $P$ by the walk condition alone (membership follows only insofar as the adjacency condition forces it).

Unfolding `Adj`: points $u, v$ are adjacent on $P$ iff $u \ne v$ **and** the closed segment $[u, v]$ is an **extreme subset** of $P$, meaning: $[u, v] \subseteq P$, and for any two points $x_1, x_2 \in P$, if some point of $[u, v]$ lies in the open segment between $x_1$ and $x_2$, then both $x_1$ and $x_2$ belong to $[u, v]$.

Edge cases the quantifiers silently include: the constants $c, k$ are chosen **uniformly, before** $d$, $n$, $a$, $b$ — a single pair must work for all dimensions and all inequality systems. If $P$ has no extreme points, $\mathrm{DiamLE}$ holds vacuously (the two outer quantifiers range over an empty set). If $c = 0$ the bound $B$ is $0$, in which case $\mathrm{DiamLE}(P, 0)$ demands $w_0 = u$ and $w_0 = v$, i.e. that $P$ has at most one extreme point; so the existential statement implicitly requires choosing $c \ge 1$ (or the bound large enough) whenever some admissible $P$ has two or more extreme points. Because stationary steps ($w_i = w_{i+1}$) are allowed, the condition is that the graph distance between any two extreme points is **at most** $B$, i.e. the combinatorial diameter of the vertex–edge graph of $P$ is $\le c\,(n+d)^k$, and in particular that this graph is connected between every pair of extreme points.

The declaration's proof is left as `sorry` (it is stated, not proved).
